messages:
Alex: FYI I'm hitting a weird TS error when building the sample edge app — works in node but fails in the edge runtime build
Maria: Gist of the error?
Alex: It complains about overloads + generics. Example: 
Alex: `function call<T>(opts: {input: T}): Promise<string>; function call(opts: {input: unknown}): Promise<string>;` -> inference ends up as 'unknown' and downstream cast fails in our SDK typings
Sam: Are you bundling with esbuild/tsc? Edge CI uses esbuild target=esnext/esm which exposes different resolution semantics
Alex: esbuild + tsc check. tsconfig has "module": "ESNext" and "esModuleInterop": true. Locally if I flip to `module: commonjs` it compiles but we can't ship CJS to worker
Lee: Sounds like two problems: overload ordering + exported type shapes that rely on `any` inference. Edge build uses stronger strict settings in CI (we enabled `noImplicitAny` + `useUnknownInCatchVariables` recently)
Maria: Could be our SDK's declaration file using `export =` somewhere, which screws ESM imports in workers. Do you see `Cannot use import statement outside a module` or `has no default export`?
Alex: Not that. It's purely a typing error: `TS2322: Type 'unknown' is not assignable to type 'T'` when calling `client.call({input: {foo: 'bar'}})` even though it should infer `T`
Sam: We've seen inference break when overloads are too permissive. Try making the generic overload more specific first, e.g. put the generic signature first so inference prefers it, or add a helper generic `callAs<T>(...)` wrapper as a workaround
Lee: Another approach: narrow the API surface in types by avoiding `unknown` in public overloads. Replace `unknown` with `any` in overloads only, then use stricter internal checks. It's safe for DX but may hide some regressions.
Maria: I'd rather not teach users to use `any`. Could we update our tsconfig for samples to set `skipLibCheck: true` and `preserveValueImports`? That often fixes weird cross-package inference issues when mixing ESM/CJS typings
Alex: Tried skipLibCheck, didn't help. I added an explicit generic when calling: `client.call<{foo:string}>({input: {foo:'bar'}})` and that silences it. But onboarding docs shouldn't require explicit generics everywhere
Sam: For edge runtimes we should also ensure `types` in package.json point to an ESM-friendly bundle. Confirm we publish `.d.ts` alongside ESM output and that `package.json` has `exports` mapping for `import`/`require` consumers
Lee: Agreed. We should also add a tiny sample tsconfig for Cloudflare Workers that sets `module: esnext`, `moduleResolution: bundler` and `target: es2020` and include a note about TypeScript 5.x differences
Maria: CI note: ci-bot: run types-check on `samples/edge-quickstart` with TS=5.1 and report failures
ci-bot: queued types check for samples/edge-quickstart on node 18 + ts@5.1
Alex: My temporary patch: add function overloads that use `T extends unknown ? T : never` nonsense to coax inference — ugly but works; I'll open a PR with tests demonstrating failure and the helper wrapper fix
Sam: We should also add a short section in SDK docs: "When to add explicit generics" + examples for edge runtimes and for CJS/ESM consumers
Maria: Can someone capture the minimal repro into a playground link or repo? That will make the TS narrow fix easier to review
Alex: I'll push a tiny repro repo to the samples org tonight and link here
Lee: Nice. For product parity: once we have repro, we should check both ESM and CJS builds for the SDK and publish a canary with the typing tweak so customers on dedicated/private aren't blocked
Maria: Also file an issue to evaluate whether `unknown` in our public API is intentional vs historical — if it's historical, we should tighten types or add explicit overloads
Alex: Thanks. I'll follow up with the PR + repro. Will ping when CI finishes
Sam: lgtm, thanks Alex :thumbsup:
Lee: small reminder — update sample's tsconfig in the repo to reduce onboarding friction (people copy it)
Alex: noted, will include it in PR
